So I was just thinking about the concept of default subs and the influence over the total site that is garnered by being classified as a default and people being auto subscribed to it.

I think it would make sense to have people autosubscribed to only things like introductions, ideasforvoat, and a few other very specific site related subs but then leave the rest of the subscriptions totally up to the user.

Now, what does this mean for the "front page" so to speak.

I think it might make sense to separate out the site's front page and the users front page. So your front page would function the same as the current, where its based on your subscriptions.

The site front page would be based on an algorithm and is based on maybe the 20 most proportionately active subs at any given time. This could be figured out by doing some calculation based on activity / subscribers.

Whether it be based on total votes, comments, something else, or some interesting combination of factors. You should be able to derive a score based on this "score" number / the number of subscribed users and get some kind of proportionally accurate list of active subs.

Then the front page is going to show just content from the most active locations and will be constantly changing.

Rough idea still, but what are your thoughts?
